Sample Name: General Medicine Followup - Advanced Kidney Disease
Description: Hyperkalemia surveillance and discussion of dialysis in a patient with severe renal impairment.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: The patient presents for routine follow-up with advanced chronic kidney disease. He reports relatively stable symptoms and continued urine output, but is reluctant to pursue dialysis because of the time and burden of treatment. Nephrology previously advised treatment of high serum potassium with sodium polystyrene sulfonate (Kayexalate), which he has available but has not been taking consistently. He needs refills of several medications, including calcium carbonate, and does not know the date of his next renal appointment. Home glucose readings are generally around 90 to 100, although occasional measurements have been reported in the 50s. He reports adherence to most chronic medications. Blood pressure is controlled.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: Advanced chronic kidney disease, hyperkalemia, hypertension and diabetes mellitus.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:
1. Advanced kidney disease: Discussed progressive renal failure and future dialysis needs. The patient remains apprehensive but will consider the recommendation. Reestablish timely Nephrology follow-up.
2. Hyperkalemia: Reinforced prescribed Kayexalate and dietary potassium restriction. Obtain immediate repeat potassium measurement; patient instructed to return and wait for result because of risk of dangerous elevation.
3. Hypertension: Continue current well-controlled regimen.
4. Diabetes: Review glucose log and monitor for hypoglycemia.
5. Medication reconciliation: Refill calcium carbonate and other required medications.
Urgent laboratory testing arranged today, followed by in-clinic review of potassium results.
